prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: 2024年重点信息化项目执行情况汇总表 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "项目" · longest unbreakable word 22px · one-line width 215px
  col 2: header "负责人" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 46px
  col 3: header "预算（万元）" · longest unbreakable word 60px · one-line width 92px
  col 4: header "进度" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 373px
  col 5: header "风险说明" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 1830px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"good","why":"All five headers sit on one line and 项目 (~147px) comfortably holds two-line project names, but 风险说明 — the column carrying roughly five times the text of any other — is the narrowest of the balanced variants (~260px), so it breaks into many short lines and inflates every row, leaving 负责人/预算 with large empty gaps."},"B":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Proportions follow the content: 项目 ~142px, 负责人 ~75px, 预算 ~105px (header still on one line), 进度 ~135px, and the dominant 风险说明 gets the largest share (~265px). Names stay horizontal, numbers stay intact, and rows are visibly shorter than in A while the left columns are not over-fed."},"C":{"grade":"good","why":"Readable and well ordered, but it squeezes 项目 to ~132px and 负责人 to ~65px without giving 风险说明 more room than B, so project titles wrap slightly more and the risk text is no better off — a small loss for no gain."},"D":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Very close to B: 风险说明 is the widest of the balanced set (~280px) so the bulk of the reading matter gets the space it needs, while 项目 (~142px) still takes two lines, 进度 ~135px reads cleanly, and 负责人 at ~65px still holds three-character names on one line."},"E":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"The risk column is cramped for its volume and the rows grow very tall; the short left columns (项目, 负责人, 预算) end up as mostly white space, so a row no longer reads as a unit and the eye has to travel far to pair a risk note with its project. Structure is intact, rhythm is not."},"F":{"grade":"poor","why":"Risk text finally gets room, but at the cost of the identifying columns: 项目 is crushed to ~90px, the header 负责人 stacks vertically and names read character-by-character (李/建/国), 预算（万元）breaks awkwardly, and 进度 is so narrow that short phrases become vertical strips — the table can no longer be scanned by project or owner."}},"best":["B","D"],"confidence":"medium","unsure":"Exact column widths are estimated from the rendered images (A–D differ by only ~10–20px per column), so B and D may be effectively the same layout; also unknown whether the target is screen or A4 print, which could shift the ideal balance slightly toward a wider 项目 column."}
